title: Alfred Jewel
blurb: 51°22′29″N 2°26′27″W / 51.374687°N 2.440724°W / 51.374687; -2.440724 The Alfred Jewel is a piece of Anglo-Saxon goldsmithing work made of enamel and quartz enclosed in gold.

title: Ascot tie
blurb: An ascot tie, or simply ascot, is an article of neckwear with wide pointed wings at the end, wrapped around the neck and draped down the chest to cover the front placket and button line of a dress shirt.

title: Aviator sunglasses
blurb: Teardrop-shaped lenses in a thin metal frame, developed in the 1930s to protect pilots' eyes.

title: Balaclava
about: Woollen cap covering the head and neck
blurb: A balaclava, also called a ski mask or racing mask, is a piece of cloth headgear designed to expose only part of the face, usually the eyes and mouth. Depending on style and how it is worn, only the eyes, mouth and nose, or just the front of the face are unprotected.

title: Bandana
blurb: A square of printed cotton, usually paisley, tied around the head, neck or wrist.

title: Baseball cap
blurb: A baseball cap is a type of soft hat with a rounded crown and a stiff bill projecting in front. The front of the hat typically displays a design or a logo.

title: Bead
about: Small decorative object with central hole
blurb: A bead is a small, decorative object that is formed in a variety of shapes and sizes of a material such as stone, bone, shell, glass, plastic, wood, or pearl and with a small hole for threading or stringing. Beads range in size from under 1 mm to over 1 cm in diameter.

title: Belt
about: Worn band or braid, usually around the waist or hips
blurb: A belt is a flexible band or strap, typically made of leather, plastic, or heavy cloth, worn around the natural waist or near it. Belts are worn to keep clothing in place or for aesthetic reasons.

title: Beret
blurb: A soft, round, flat-crowned wool cap worn by shepherds, soldiers and painters.

title: Blue Elephant
blurb: Blue Elephant is a South Korean brand of eyewear, including sunglasses and optical frames. The brand was founded in 2019 as an online business and later expanded into physical retail locations in South Korea, Japan, the Philippines, and the United States.

title: Bonnet
about: Large semicircular head covering framing the face; alternatively, a brimless hat or cap
blurb: Bonnet has been used as the name for a wide variety of headgear for women since the Middle Ages.[citation needed] As with "hat" and "cap", it is impossible to generalize styles for which the word has been used, there is a tendency to describe it having soft material and lacking a brim, or at least…

title: Bow tie
blurb: A ribbon of fabric tied in a symmetrical bow at the collar, favoured by professors and magicians.

title: Bowler hat
about: Hard, round-crowned hat with a narrow rolled brim
blurb: The bowler hat, also known as a Coke hat, billycock, bob hat, or derby, is a hard felt hat with a rounded crown, originally created by the London hat-makers Thomas and William Bowler in 1849 and commissioned by Lock & Co. Hatters of St James's Street, London.

title: Bracelet
blurb: A bracelet is an article of jewellery that is worn around the wrist. Bracelets may serve different uses, such as being worn as an ornament. When worn as ornaments, bracelets may have a supportive function to hold other items of decoration, such as charms.

title: Brooch
about: Large ornament with a pin fastening
blurb: A brooch is a decorative jewellery item, or the insignia of a fraternal order, designed to be attached to garments, often to fasten them together. It is usually made of metal, often silver or gold or some other material.

title: Bug-eye glasses
blurb: Bug-eye glasses are a form of eyewear. They were popular in the 1970s, 1980s and 1990s, and were used for regular glasses and sunglasses. They first became popular in the mid-1970s, and succeeded the cat eye glasses of the 1950s and 1960s.

title: Charm bracelet
blurb: A bracelet hung with small trinkets, each one marking a place, a person or a memory.

title: Chatelaine
blurb: A chatelaine is a decorative belt hook or clasp worn at the waist with a series of chains suspended from it. Each chain is mounted with useful household appendages such as scissors, thimbles, watches, keys, smelling salts, and household seals.

title: Claddagh ring
blurb: A Claddagh ring is a traditional Irish ring with three primary features: a heart to represent love, a crown to represent loyalty, and two clasped hands to symbolise friendship. The design and customs associated with it originated in Claddagh, County Galway.

title: Coif
blurb: A coif is a close fitting headdress or cap worn by both men and women that covers the top, back, and sides of the head.

title: Coronet
blurb: In British heraldry, a coronet is a type of crown that is a mark of rank of non-reigning members of the royal family and peers. In other languages, this distinction is not made, and usually the same word for crown is used irrespective of rank.

title: Costa Del Mar
blurb: Costa Del Mar or simply Costa is a manufacturer of polarized sunglasses based in Daytona Beach. Luxottica closed the facility when they purchased the brand. It is a wholly owned subsidiary of EssilorLuxottica.

title: Cowboy hat
blurb: The cowboy hat is a high-crowned, wide-brimmed hat best known as the defining piece of attire for the North American cowboy.

title: Cravat
about: Long strip of fine cloth wound around the neck and tied in front into a bow or knot
blurb: The cravat is a neckband, the forerunner of the modern tailored necktie and bow tie, originating from a style worn by members of the 17th century military unit known as the Cravats. The modern British "cravat" is called an "ascot tie" in American English.

title: Crown jewels
about: Objects of metalwork and jewellery in the regalia of a current or former monarchy
blurb: Crown jewels are the objects of metalwork and jewellery in the regalia of a current or former monarchy. They are often used for the coronation of a monarch and a few other ceremonial occasions.

title: Crown Jewels of the United Kingdom
blurb: The Crown Jewels of the United Kingdom, originally the Crown Jewels of England, are a collection of royal ceremonial objects kept in the Jewel House at the Tower of London, which include the coronation regalia and vestments worn by British monarchs.

title: Crown of Queen Elizabeth the Queen Mother
blurb: The Crown of Queen Elizabeth the Queen Mother, also known as the Queen Mother's Crown, is the crown made for Queen Elizabeth the Queen Mother to wear at her coronation in 1937 and State Openings of Parliament during the reign of her husband, King George VI.

title: Crown of Scotland
about: Crown that was used for coronation of monarchs of Scotland
blurb: The Crown of Scotland is the centrepiece of the Honours of Scotland. It is the crown that was used at the coronation of the monarchs of Scotland, and it is the oldest surviving crown in the British Isles and the fifth oldest in Europe.

title: Cufflink
blurb: A small decorative fastener for shirt cuffs, and a tiny canvas for personality.

title: Cullinan Diamond
blurb: The Cullinan Diamond is the largest gem-quality rough diamond ever found, weighing 3,106 carats, discovered at the Premier No.2 mine in Cullinan, South Africa, on 26 January 1905. It was named after Thomas Cullinan, the owner of the mine.

title: Cummerbund
blurb: A cummerbund is a broad waist sash, usually pleated, which is often worn with single-breasted dinner jackets. The cummerbund was adopted by British military officers in colonial India, where they saw it worn by sepoys of the British Indian Army.

title: Daria-i-Noor
blurb: The Daria-i-Noor is one of the largest cut diamonds in the world, weighing an estimated 182 carats. Its colour, pale pink, is one of the rarest to be found in diamonds. The diamond is currently in the Iranian National Jewels collection of the Central Bank of Iran in Tehran.

title: Dastar
blurb: A dastār is an item of headwear associated with Sikhism and Sikh culture. The word is loaned from Persian through Punjabi. In Persian, the word dastār can refer to any kind of turban and replaced the original word for turban, dolband, from which the English word is derived.

title: Deerstalker
blurb: A deerstalker is a type of cap that is typically worn in English rural areas, often for hunting, especially deer stalking.

title: Diadem
about: Ornamental headband worn by monarchs and others as a badge of royalty
blurb: A diadem was an ornamental headband, and later became a metal crown, worn by monarchs and others as a badge of royalty.

title: Dupatta
about: Cloth wrap worn as a shawl, scarf, or veil in the Indian Subcontinent
blurb: The dupattā, also called chunni, chunari, chundari, lugda, rao/rawo, gandhi, pothi, orna, and odhni is a long shawl-like scarf traditionally worn by both women and men in the Indian subcontinent.

title: Earring
about: Type of jewelry and body piercing
blurb: Earrings are jewelry that are worn on one's ears. Earrings are often worn through earlobe piercings or another external part of the ear, or by some other means, such as stickers or clip-ons.

title: Engagement ring
blurb: An engagement ring, also known as a betrothal ring, is a ring indicating that the person wearing it is engaged to be married, especially in Western cultures.

title: Eyewear
about: Items and accessories worn on or over the eyes
blurb: Eyewear is a term used to refer to all devices worn over both of a person's eyes, or occasionally a single eye, for one or more of a variety of purposes.

title: Fashion accessory
about: Item used to contribute to the wearer's outfit
blurb: In fashion, an accessory is an item used to contribute, in a secondary manner, to an individual's outfit. Accessories are often chosen to complete an outfit and complement the wearer's look. They have the capacity to further express an individual's identity and personality.

title: Fedora
about: Felt hat with brim and indented crown
blurb: A fedora is a hat with a soft brim and indented crown. It is typically creased lengthwise down the crown and pinched near the front on both sides. Fedoras can also be creased with teardrop crowns, diamond crowns, center dents, and others, and the positioning of pinches can vary.

title: Fez
about: Cylinder-shaped cap with a flat crown
blurb: The fez, also called tarboosh/tarboush, is a felt headdress in the shape of a short, cylindrical, peakless hat, usually red, typically with a black tassel attached to the top. The name "fez" may refer to the Moroccan city of Fez, where the dye to color the hat was extracted from crimson berries.

title: Flat cap
blurb: A flat cap is a rounded cap with a small stiff brim in front, originating in Northern England. The hat is also known in Ireland as a paddy cap; in Scotland as a bunnet or Galen's cap; in Wales as a Dai cap; and in the United States as an English cap or Irish cap. Various other terms exist.

title: Gauntlet
blurb: A gauntlet is a type of glove that protects the hand and wrist of a combatant. Gauntlets, which cover the hands, wrists, and sometimes forearms, are not to be confused with bracers, which cover the wrists and forearms but not the hands; bracers are common in medieval and fantasy cosplay.

title: Girdle
about: Belt, esp. as a liturgical vestment
blurb: A girdle is a belt without a buckle, especially if made of a cord or rope. Historically girdles were a common part of everyday clothing, from antiquity until perhaps the 15th century, especially for women.

title: Glove
blurb: A glove is a garment covering the hand, with separate sheaths or openings for each finger including the thumb. Gloves protect and comfort hands against cold or heat, damage by friction, abrasion or chemicals, and disease; or in turn to provide a guard for what a bare hand should not touch.

title: Grill
about: Type of jewelry worn on the teeth
blurb: In pop culture, a grill, also known as fronts or golds, is a type of dental jewelry worn over the teeth. Grills are made of metal and are generally removable but can also be permanent.

title: Groucho glasses
about: Novelty glasses with a nose, moustache, and eyebrows
blurb: Groucho glasses are a humorous novelty disguise which function as a caricature of the stage makeup used by the comedian Groucho Marx in his movies and vaudeville performances.

title: Hand fan
blurb: A folding or fixed fan waved by hand, sometimes painted, sometimes used to send coded messages.

title: Handkerchief
about: Piece of cloth for personal use
blurb: A handkerchief is a form of a kerchief or bandanna, typically a hemmed square of thin fabric which can be carried in the pocket or handbag for personal hygiene purposes such as wiping one's hands or face, or blowing one's nose.

title: Hat
blurb: A hat is a head covering which is worn for various reasons, including protection against weather conditions, ceremonial reasons such as university graduation, religious reasons, comedy, safety, or as a fashion accessory.

title: Head covering for Jewish women
about: Wig or half-wig worn by some married Orthodox Jewish women
blurb: According to halacha, married Orthodox Jewish women are expected to cover their hair when in the presence of men other than their husband or close family members. Such covering is common practice among Orthodox Jewish women. This is called kisui rosh.

title: Headgear
about: Any covering for the head; element of clothing which is worn on one's head
blurb: Headgear, headwear, or headdress is any element of clothing which is worn on one's head, including hats, helmets, turbans and many other types.

title: Headscarf
about: Piece of cloth worn on one's head
blurb: A headscarf is a scarf covering most or all of the top of a person's, usually women's, hair and head, leaving the face uncovered. A headscarf is formed of a triangular cloth or a square cloth folded into a triangle, with which the head is covered.

title: Helmet
blurb: A helmet is a form of protective gear worn to protect the head. More specifically, a helmet complements the skull in protecting the human brain. Ceremonial or symbolic helmets without protective function are sometimes worn.

title: Holy Crown of Hungary
about: Coronation crown used by Hungarian monarchs
blurb: The Holy Crown of Hungary, also known as the Crown of Saint Stephen, named in honour of Saint Stephen I of Hungary, was the coronation crown used by the Kingdom of Hungary for most of its existence; kings were crowned with it from the 12th century on.

title: Homburg hat
blurb: A homburg is a semi-formal hat of fur felt, characterized by a single dent running down the centre of the crown, a wide silk grosgrain hatband ribbon, a flat brim shaped in a "pencil curl", and a ribbon-bound trim about the edge of the brim. It is traditionally offered in black or grey.

title: Hope Diamond
blurb: The Hope Diamond is a 45.52-carat blue diamond that has been famed for its great size and blue-violet color since the 17th century. It was extracted in the 17th century from the Kollur Mine in Andhra Pradesh, India.

title: Imperial Crown of Russia
about: Diamond crown used by the Russian monarchs
blurb: The Imperial Crown of Russia, also known as the Great Imperial Crown of the Russian Empire, was used for the coronation of the monarchs of Russia from 1762 until the Russian monarchy's abolition in 1917.

title: Imperial Crown of the Holy Roman Empire
about: Crown worn by the Holy Roman Emperor
blurb: The Imperial Crown of the Holy Roman Empire, a hoop crown with a characteristic octagonal shape, was the coronation crown of the Holy Roman Emperor, probably from the late 10th century until the dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire in 1806.

title: Imperial State Crown
about: One of the Crown Jewels of the United Kingdom
blurb: The Imperial State Crown is the state crown of the British monarch. Based on the design of Queen Victoria's Crown of 1838, which had fallen into disrepair, it was made in 1937 for the coronation of King George VI. The crown remains in use today at coronations and State Openings of Parliament.

title: Iron Crown
blurb: The Iron Crown is a reliquary votive crown, traditionally considered one of the oldest royal insignia of Christendom.

title: Iron Ring
blurb: The Iron Ring is a ring worn by many Canadian engineers as a symbol and reminder of the obligations and ethics associated with their profession. The ring is presented in a private ceremony known as the Ritual of the Calling of an Engineer.

title: Japamala
blurb: A japamala, jaap maala, or simply mala is a loop of prayer beads commonly used in Indian religions such as Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism and Sikhism. It is used for counting recitations of mantras, prayers or other sacred phrases.

title: Jewellery
blurb: Jewellery consists of decorative items worn for personal adornment such as brooches, rings, necklaces, earrings, pendants, bracelets, and cufflinks. Jewellery may be attached to the body or the clothes.

title: Kasa
blurb: A kasa is any one of several traditional Japanese hats. Examples include amigasa and jingasa.

title: Keffiyeh
about: Traditional headdress worn by men in the Middle East
blurb: The keffiyeh, also regionally known as a hattah, ghutrah, shemagh, or chafiyeh is a traditional headdress worn by men from parts of the Middle East and North Africa. It is fashioned from a square scarf, and is usually made of cotton.

title: Kepi
about: Flat circular cap with a visor
blurb: The kepi is a cap with a flat circular top and a peak, or visor. In English, the term is a loanword from French: képi, itself a re-spelled version of the Alemannic German: Käppi, a diminutive form of Kappe, meaning 'cap'.

title: Knit cap
blurb: A knit cap is a piece of knitted headwear designed to provide warmth in cold weather. It usually has a simple tapered shape, although more elaborate variants exist. Historically made of wool, it is now often made of synthetic fibers.

title: Koh-i-Noor
blurb: The Koh-i-Noor is one of the largest cut diamonds in the world, weighing 105.6 carats. It is currently set in the Crown of Queen Elizabeth the Queen Mother. The earliest recorded history dates to the late 15th century, when it came into the possession of Babur, founder of the Mughal Empire.

title: Kokoshnik
about: Traditional Russian headdress worn by women
blurb: The kokoshnik is a traditional Russian headdress worn by women and girls to accompany the sarafan. The kokoshnik tradition has existed since the 10th century in the city of Veliky Novgorod. It spread primarily in the northern regions of Russia and was very popular from 16th to 19th centuries.

title: Kufi
about: Cap worn primarily by both Muslim men, and men of West African heritage
blurb: A kufi or kufi cap is a brimless, short, and rounded cap worn by men in many populations in North, East, and West Africa, South Asia, and the Middle East. It is also worn by men throughout the African diaspora. The cap has strong associations with many Islamic cultures and pan-African pride.

title: La Peregrina pearl
about: Pearl formerly owned by Spanish monarchs
blurb: The La Peregrina pearl is one of the most famous pearls in the world. Its owners include the Spanish monarchs, the history of the pearl spans almost 500 years and recently belonged to actress Elizabeth Taylor. The jewel is now in private ownership.

title: Mangalasutra
about: Necklace, tied around the bride's neck in Hindu weddings
blurb: A mangala sutra, or tali, is a necklace worn by certain groups of married women from the Indian subcontinent.

title: Maui Jim
blurb: Maui Jim is an American sunglasses manufacturer based in Peoria, Illinois. Founded in Lahaina, Hawaii, in 1980, the company designs, develops, and manufactures a wide variety of sunglasses marketed under the eponymous brand name.

title: Mirrored sunglasses
blurb: Mirrored sunglasses are sunglasses with a reflective optical coating on the outside of the lenses to make them appear like small mirrors. The lenses typically give the wearer's vision a brown or grey tint.

title: Monocle
blurb: A single corrective lens held in the eye socket, now mostly worn by cartoon aristocrats.

title: Moscot
blurb: Moscot is an American eyewear company based in New York City. Founded on Manhattan's Lower East Side in 1915 by Hyman Moscot, it developed from a neighborhood optical shop into a family-owned eyewear business with retail locations in the United States and internationally.

title: Neck ring
blurb: Neck rings, or neck-rings, are any form of stiff jewellery worn as an ornament around the neck of an individual, as opposed to a loose necklace. Many cultures and periods have made neck rings, with both males and females wearing them at various times.

title: Necklace
blurb: A necklace is an article of jewellery that is worn around the neck. Necklaces may have been one of the earliest types of adornment worn by humans.

title: Necktie
about: Clothing item worn around the neck
blurb: A necktie – also called a long tie or, more usually, simply a tie – is a cloth article of formal neckwear or office attire worn for decorative or symbolic purposes, knotted at the throat, resting under a folded shirt collar, and usually draped down the chest.

title: Newsboy cap
about: Headgear similar to a flat cap
blurb: The newsboy cap, newsie cap, Gatsby, jeff cap, or baker boy hat is a casual-wear cap similar in style to the flat cap.

title: Oakley, Inc.
about: Manufacturer of sports eyewear owned by EssilorLuxottica
blurb: Oakley, Inc. is a company headquartered in Foothill Ranch, California, which is an autonomous subsidiary of the Italian eyewear group Luxottica.

title: Obi
about: Sash worn with traditional Japanese clothing and Japanese martial arts uniforms
blurb: An obi is a sash of varying size and shape worn with both traditional Japanese clothing and uniforms for Japanese martial arts styles.

title: Panama hat
blurb: A light straw hat hand-woven in Ecuador, despite the name, from toquilla palm.

title: Papakha
blurb: The papakha is a sheepskin hat worn by men throughout the Caucasus and also in uniformed military regiments in the region and beyond.

title: Papal tiara
about: Crown worn by popes of the Roman Catholic Church
blurb: The papal tiara is a crown that was worn by popes of the Catholic Church from as early as the 8th century to the mid–20th century. It was last used by Pope Paul VI in 1963, and only at the beginning of his reign.

title: Patiala Necklace
blurb: The Patiala Necklace was a necklace designed and made by Cartier in 1928. It was part of the largest single order ever placed with Cartier to date, made in 1925 by the Indian royal Bhupinder Singh, the Maharaja of Patiala, for the Patiala Necklace and other jewellery worth ₹1,000 million.

title: Peaked cap
blurb: A peaked cap, peaked hat, service cap, barracks cover, forage cap, or combination cap is a form of headgear worn by the armed forces of many nations, as well as many uniformed civilian organisations such as law enforcement agencies and fire departments.

title: Pearl
about: Hard object produced within a living shelled mollusc
blurb: A pearl is a hard, shiny object produced within the soft tissue of a living shelled mollusk. Like the shell of a mollusk, a pearl is composed of calcium carbonate in a crystalline form, which is deposited in concentric layers.

title: Pearl necklace
blurb: A strand of pearls, worn in lengths with names like choker, princess, matinee and opera.

title: Persol
about: Sports eyewear company owned by EssilorLuxottica
blurb: Persol is an Italian luxury eyewear brand specializing in the manufacturing of sunglasses and optical frames. It is one of the oldest eyewear companies in the world and is owned by the Luxottica group. The name is derived from the Italian per il sole, meaning "for the sun".

title: Phrygian cap
about: Soft conical cap with the top pulled forward
blurb: The Phrygian capən/ ), also known as Thracian cap and liberty cap, is a soft conical cap with the apex bent over, associated in antiquity with several peoples in Eastern Europe, Anatolia, and Asia.

title: Pileus
about: Felt conical or half-egg-shaped cap, worn in Ancient Greece, Rome and by ecclesiastics
blurb: The pileus was a brimless felt cap worn in Ancient Greece, Etruria, Illyria, later also introduced in Ancient Rome. The pileus also appears on Apulian red-figure pottery. The pilos and petasos were the most common types of hats in Archaic and Classical era Greece.

title: Pinhole glasses
blurb: The effect of pinhole glasses approximated by a camera Pinhole glasses, also known as stenopeic glasses, are eyeglasses with a series of pinhole-sized perforations filling an opaque sheet of plastic in place of each lens.

title: Pork pie hat
blurb: A pork pie hat is one of several different styles of hat that have been worn since the mid-19th century. The pork pie hat gained further popularity in the 20th century, being worn by famous actors and musicians.

title: Ray-Ban
blurb: Ray-Ban is an American Italian-owned brand of luxury sunglasses and standard glasses created in 1936 by Canadian international company Bausch & Lomb. The brand is most notable for its Wayfarer and Aviator lines of sunglasses.

title: Regent Diamond
about: 140.64-carat (28.128 g) diamond owned by the French state
blurb: The Regent Diamond is a 140.64-carat diamond owned by the French state and on display in the Louvre, worth US$60,000,000 as of 2025[update]. Mined in India and cut in London, it was purchased by the regent of France in the early 18th century.

title: Rhinestone
blurb: A rhinestone, paste or diamanté is a diamond simulant originally made from rock crystal but since the 19th century from crystal glass or polymers such as acrylic.

title: Safilo
blurb: Safilo Group S.p.A. is an Italian company that designs, produces, and distributes prescription frames, sunglasses, sports eyewear, ski goggles and helmets, and cycling helmets under its own five house brands and 32 licensed brands, including Smith Optics since 1996.

title: Samsung Galaxy Glasses
blurb: The Samsung Galaxy Glasses is an upcoming product designed, developed, manufactured, and marketed by Samsung Electronics, as the part of the Samsung Galaxy series.

title: Sancy
about: Historic diamond once part of English crown jewels
blurb: The Sancy, a pale yellow diamond of 55.23 carats, was reputed to have belonged to the Mughal emperors, and is at least probably Indian in origin owing to its cut, which is unusual by Western standards.

title: Sash
about: Band of fabric worn on the body
blurb: A sash is a large and usually colorful ribbon or band of material worn around the human body, either draping from one shoulder to the opposing hip and back up, or else encircling the waist.

title: Scarf
about: Garment of fabric worn around neck or head
blurb: A scarf is a long piece of fabric that is worn on or around the neck, shoulders, or head. A scarf is used for warmth, sun protection, cleanliness, fashion, religious reasons, or to show support for a sports club or team. Scarves can be made from materials including wool, linen, silk, and cotton.

title: Shtreimel
about: Fur hat worn by married Hasidic Jewish men
blurb: A shtreimel is a fur hat worn by some Ashkenazi Jewish men, mainly members of Hasidic Judaism, on Shabbat and Jewish holidays and other festive occasions. In Jerusalem, the shtreimel is also worn by Litvak Jews.

title: Shutter shades
blurb: Shutter shades, also known as slatted shades, louvered shades, or Venetian blind shades are sunglasses that, instead of having darkened lenses, have horizontal slats similar to window shutters, which are an integral part of the frame.[citation needed] The shades are available in an assortment of…

title: Signet ring
blurb: A ring engraved with a crest or initials, once pressed into hot wax to seal a letter.

title: Silhouette
blurb: Silhouette International Schmied AG is an eyewear company headquartered in Linz, Austria. Since 2017, the company is a full-service provider for both frames and lenses. Since 2008, the company has been a state-awarded training company.

title: Smartglasses
blurb: Smartglasses or smart glasses are eye or head-worn wearable computers. Many smartglasses include displays that add information alongside or to what the wearer sees.

title: Solar viewer
blurb: Solar viewers are special eyewear designed for direct viewing of the Sun. Standard sunglasses are unable to filter out eye-damaging radiation. Solar viewers can be used for safe viewing of solar events such as eclipses.

title: St Edward's Crown
about: Part of the Crown Jewels of the United Kingdom
blurb: St Edward's Crown is the coronation crown of the Crown Jewels of the United Kingdom. Named after Edward the Confessor, versions of it have traditionally been used to crown English and British monarchs at their coronations since the 13th century.

title: Stetson
blurb: Stetson is an American brand of hat manufactured by the John B. Stetson Company. John B. Stetson gained inspiration for his most famous hats when he headed west from his native New Jersey for health reasons. On his return east in 1865, he founded the John B. Stetson Company in Philadelphia.

title: Sunglasses
about: Eyewear for protecting against bright light
blurb: Sunglasses or sun glasses are a form of protective eyewear designed primarily to prevent bright sunlight and high-energy visible light from damaging or discomforting the eyes.

title: Tam o' shanter
blurb: A tam o' shanter or "tammie" is a name given to the traditional Scottish bonnet worn by men. The name derives from Tam o' Shanter, the eponymous hero of the 1790 Robert Burns poem.

title: Taqiyah
about: Short rounded skullcap worn by some Muslims
blurb: The Taqiyah, also known as tagiyah or araqchin, is a short, rounded skullcap worn by Muslim men. In the United States and the United Kingdom, it is also referred to as a "kufi", although the kufi typically has more of an African connotation while the taqiyah has a more universal connotation.

title: Tiara
blurb: A jewelled half-crown worn at the front of the head on very grand occasions.

title: Top hat
blurb: A top hat is a tall, flat-crowned hat traditionally associated with formal wear in Western dress codes, meaning white tie, morning dress, or frock coat. Traditionally made of black silk or sometimes grey, the top hat emerged in Western fashion by the end of the 18th century.

title: Torc
about: Rigid, usually twisted ring worn around the neck or arm, often of precious metal
blurb: A torc, also spelled torq or torque, is a large rigid or stiff neck ring in metal, made either as a single piece or from strands twisted together. The great majority are open at the front, although some have hook and ring closures and a few have mortice and tenon locking catches to close them.

title: Toupée
about: Hairpiece or partial wig of natural or synthetic hair
blurb: A toupée is a hairpiece or partial wig of natural or synthetic hair worn to cover partial baldness or for theatrical purposes. While toupées and hairpieces are typically associated with male wearers, some women also use hairpieces to lengthen existing hair, or cover a partially exposed scalp.

title: Trilby
blurb: A trilby is a narrow-brimmed type of hat. The trilby was once viewed as the rich man's favoured hat; it is sometimes called the "brown trilby" in Britain and was frequently seen at the horse races.

title: Tudor Crown
about: Crown of Tudor monarchs and heraldic device
blurb: The Tudor Crown, also known as the Imperial Crown, was a crown created in the early 16th century for either Henry VII or Henry VIII, the first Tudor monarchs of England, and destroyed in 1649 during the English Civil War.

title: Turban
blurb: A turban is a type of headwear based on cloth winding. Featuring many variations, it is worn as customary headwear by people of various cultures.

title: Umbrella
blurb: A folding canopy on a stick, for rain or sun, and one of the most frequently lost objects on earth.

title: Ushanka
about: Russian fur cap with ear flaps
blurb: An ushanka, also called an ushanka-hat, is a Russian fur hat with ear-covering flaps that can be tied up on the crown of the cap, or fastened at the chin to protect the ears, jaw, and lower chin from the cold.

title: Vuarnet
blurb: Vuarnet is a premium heritage brand of sunglasses founded in 1957 that is owned by French manufacturer Sporoptic Pouilloux S.A. Thélios acquired Sporoptic Pouilloux S.A. and Vuarnet in 2023.

title: War bonnet
blurb: War bonnets are feathered headgear traditionally worn by male leaders of the American Plains Indian Nations who have earned a place of great respect in their tribe. Originally they were sometimes worn into battle, but they are now primarily used for ceremonial occasions.

title: Wedding ring
about: Finger ring which indicates that its wearer is married
blurb: A wedding ring, also called a wedding band in the United States, is a finger ring that indicates that its wearer is married. It is usually forged from metal, traditionally gold or another precious metal. Rings were used in ancient Rome during marriage.

title: Wig
blurb: A wig is a head covering made from human or animal hair, or a synthetic imitation thereof. The word is short for "periwig", derived from the French word perruque. Wigs may be worn to disguise baldness, to alter the wearer's appearance, or as part of certain professional uniforms.

title: Wimple
blurb: A wimple is a medieval form of female headcovering, formed of a large piece of cloth worn draped around the neck and chin, covering the top of the head; it was usually made from white linen or silk.

title: X-ray specs
blurb: X-ray specs or X-ray glasses are an American novelty item, purported to allow users to see through or into solid objects. In reality, the spectacles merely create an optical illusion; no X-rays are involved.
